correctness.rationale: Paths are Cartesian-prime; automorphisms of a Cartesian power are generated by coordinate reflections and permutations, so full nearest-end-distance histograms are the orbits. For n>=3, the initial degree 2d−c_0 gives round one. At any t<r, the neighbour multiset of a truncated histogram H_t depends only on H_{t+1}; crucially, the multiplicity of neighbours increasing the previous count c_{t−1} by one (without changing earlier counts) is exactly c_t. Hence round t+1 recovers exactly one additional histogram coordinate and no extra data. Since c_r is the remainder, round r reaches the orbit partition and is stable; two vectors differing only at categories r−1 and r show strictness at previous round. Odd/even central-layer multiplicities produce the orbit sizes. An independent full-graph 1-WL implementation verified 39 configurations covering 10,899 vertices, including all intermediate partitions; the general induction is required beyond that finite check.

value.rationale: The theorem exactly solves every round and stabilization time for a canonical family of grids of arbitrary Cartesian dimension, revealing the dimension-independent boundary-radius depth while also determining every stable cell size. This is meaningful structural 1-WL information, not merely a numerical benchmark.

final_claim: For P_n^□d (n>=2,d>=1) with uniform initial colouring, set r=floor((n−1)/2); after exactly t rounds for 0<=t<=r, colours distinguish precisely the coordinate nearest-end-distance histogram counts c_0,...,c_{t−1}. The first stable round is r; stable classes are exactly vertex automorphism orbits, number binomial(d+r,r), and each orbit has the explicit multinomial central-coordinate multiplicity formula. For n=2 stabilization is round 0.
